ROLE: Perform the single legal forward transition from AWAITING_CONNECT to READY after an accepted CONNECT, so protocol traffic is admitted only on a connected session.

VAR.NAME: SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT
VAR.ROLE: the only state that may become READY

VAR.NAME: SESSION_READY
VAR.ROLE: target state after an accepted CONNECT

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSING
VAR.ROLE: must not be pulled back to READY

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSED
VAR.ROLE: terminal, must not be pulled back to READY

LOGIC.INPUT: s: borrowed session pointer, possibly NULL.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If s is NULL return. 2) If s->state != SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT do nothing: the session is already READY (a second CONNECT is a protocol error handled by the caller), CLOSING (queued output is flushing, no new protocol input is accepted) or CLOSED (terminal). Applying the transition unconditionally would resurrect a closing session and cause the write pump to keep a descriptor the reaper already owns — so this guard is the state-machine invariant. 3) Otherwise set s->state = SESSION_READY. Only the state changes; the descriptor, buffers and queued CONNACK are untouched, and the CONNACK bytes are queued by the caller either before or after this call.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: No return value. A session in AWAITING_CONNECT becomes READY; every other session is unchanged.
INVARIANTS_USED: the only legal transition into READY is AWAITING_CONNECT -> READY
CLOSED is terminal and CLOSING accepts no new protocol input
state changes must not alter ownership of the descriptor or the buffers
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is NULL or points to a live session.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: s->state is SESSION_READY when it was SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT before the call; otherwise unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe with respect to concurrent transitions on s.
